description: The language and guild domain trees as a skill panel draws them, and a saved skills block restored into SkillProgression with the effects of the nodes taken (src/skills/, src/game-engine/logic/SkillProgression.ts). The skill KB sees the live facts (PL.core-skill-kb-live-facts, src/progression/skill-kb.ts; appended): the program a recomposing host consults (op compose) and a skill session through asserts, retracts, saves and loads, answering unlocks (op kb; docs/progression-systems.md section 6). A live fact naming a rule head the skill pack defines is never live (skill_owned; PL.core-skill-kb-rule-head-facts, appended).
comparison: exact, object key sets included (a key TypeScript leaves undefined is absent); an unknown op or step is an error, never a skip

cases.name: compose: the live predicates are declared dynamic before the world and the live clauses follow it, in clause order (PL.core-skill-kb-live-facts)

cases.name: compose: a predicate the engine owns is dropped (reserved), and a number in exponent form is written in Prolog's syntax (PL.core-skill-kb-live-facts)
cases.note: member/2 is a library predicate of the shared engine: a recomposing host that consulted member(player, smiths_guild) would fail with permission_error(modify, static_procedure, member/2). 1e-7 is not a Prolog number; 1.0e-7 is.

cases.name: kb: a fact the KB cannot hold is never live: a predicate the engine owns is reserved, a control character is unreadable, and an exponent number is held (PL.core-skill-kb-live-facts)
cases.note: member/2, length/2 and true/0 are the engine's (builtin or library) and attribute/1 is a prefix operator's name, so the KB cannot hold them: a load drops each (reserved), an assert or retract changes nothing, and guild_apprentice, permitted by reputation 25, stays permitted throughout. A string holding a newline is unreadable. gold(player, 1e-7) and gold(player, 1e+21) are live, held as 1.0e-7 and 1.0e+21, and a save keeps them as numbers.

cases.name: compose: a fact naming a rule head the skill pack defines is skill_owned; the same name at another arity is live (PL.core-skill-kb-rule-head-facts)
cases.note: can_advance/2, can_learn_skill/2, can_unlock/2, skill_capped/2, skill_effect/2, skill_goal_met/2, skill_node_price/2 and skill_points_held/3 are the rule heads of core's skill pack (src/prolog/mechanics/skill-predicates.ts; SKILL_KB_PACK_RULE_HEADS reads them from its clauses): a live clause of one would be a clause added to the pack's rule. The refusal is the same whatever pack a host hands compose. skill_goal_met/1, can_unlock/1, skill_points_held/2 and can_advance/3 are other predicates, and are live.

:- dynamic(has_skill/3).

:- dynamic(can_advance/3).
:- dynamic(can_unlock/1).
:- dynamic(skill_goal_met/1).
:- dynamic(skill_points_held/2).
w(1).

can_advance(player, french, soon).
can_unlock(player).
skill_goal_met(bridge_repaired).
skill_points_held(player, 9).

cases.name: kb: a fact naming a rule head the skill pack defines is never live, so an atom requirement holds only when its atom does (PL.core-skill-kb-rule-head-facts)
cases.note: guild_bridgewarden requires the plain atom bridge_repaired, which the pack's skill_goal_met/2 calls as written. skill_goal_met(player, bridge_repaired) and can_unlock(player, guild_master) name rule heads of the pack, so they are dropped at the load (skill_owned) and an assert or retract of one changes nothing: held, each would be a clause added to the pack's rule (a KB that answers a held fact before the rule would meet the atom requirement with the bridge unrepaired). skill_goal_met/1 and can_unlock/1 are other predicates: they load, and do not open the node. Only bridge_repaired does.
